choices_after_data: H9 itself was conceived after seeing that every established pentaquark carries c cbar (SM7's honesty note); those states are not evidence for it.

The claimed-pentaquark list was compiled from the claims we could find and verify on arXiv; light hidden-flavour candidates are not claimed as pentaquarks in the literature we read, so the table has no light hidden-flavour row.

I2: the molecular masses carry over binding energies relative to isospin-averaged thresholds (the lead's instruction and SM7); the reduced-mass scaling is a variant added with it, not chosen after seeing anything, since no hidden-bottom pentaquark is known.

I4: the eligibility rule and the list were written before any splitting was computed, but the masses of all candidate states were known from SM6, and the P_cs(4459) two-peak masses were read (for the status in I1) before the list was written; it is listed as not resolved by the rule. The chance null (Delta uniform in 0 to 300 MeV) and the 1.96 sigma pass criterion were fixed with the list.

The rule for binding across the two halves (primary: KR's factorised potential applied to every pair; variant P-in: no binding across the root) was written into the script before any exotic state was computed, but by authors who knew the published masses of the exotic states. Both rules are reported for every state; they differ only where a heavy or strange pair sits in different halves (hidden-charm and fully charmed states, P_c, T_csbar).

k_s (KR's heavy-strange hyperfine enhancement a_cs = a_bs) is shared between mesons and baryons. KR apply it in baryons only; the extension was fixed before the fit, motivated by KR's own observation that the D_s* - D_s splitting is enhanced by the same factor, not by any exotic comparison.

For each catalogue state one measurement was taken: the most recent one of the cited collaboration that we could read (LHCb 2021 for the J/psi phi states, not the 2016 values; the BESIII discovery values for Z_c(3900) and Z_c(4020), not PDG averages, which we could not read). The catalogue excludes X(3915) (exotic status disputed), P_cs(4459) and P_c(4337) (evidence below 5 sigma).
The chance-proximity numbers for the three 'nearest level' assignments (p_chance) were added after seeing that they hold.

Tests B5 (states with measured J^P only), B6 (without the two states within 1 MeV of a threshold) and B7 (distances floored at the mass error) were added after seeing the Fisher result, to show what drives it.

The CMS and ATLAS di-J/psi structures are shown with the fully charmed levels but not scored; that the lowest ATLAS structure (6.41 GeV) lies near the model's S-wave levels was noticed after the comparison and is not a test.
caveats: Effective-mass conventions dominate the multiquark predictions. Baryon masses for every constituent (KR) and universal masses with string junctions (variant J) differ by 90 to 113 MeV for the tetraquarks and 204 to 210 MeV for the lowest pentaquarks, ten to twenty-five times sigma_model; the fit to ordinary hadrons cannot choose between them (sigma_model 8.1 and 8.2 MeV).

sigma_model is the spread of ordinary hadrons. It does not include the uncertainty of carrying the model to four and five constituents (colour configurations outside the H8 tree, the spatial size of a diquark pair, binding across the halves).

The H8 tree keeps one colour configuration (3bar x 3 for tetraquarks). The full colour-spin model also has 6 x 6bar; mixing would lower the lowest levels, mostly for the fully heavy and hidden-charm states.
Only S-wave ground states are computed. Radial and orbital excitations (X1(2900) is 1-) are outside the model, so a mismatch refutes an S-wave assignment, not every compact reading.

Threshold test: the catalogue is not a random sample. Many exotic states were found as narrow structures near thresholds, and threshold cusps can mimic peaks, so proximity is partly a selection effect. The threshold list (hadrons narrower than 60 MeV) and the S-wave and C rules set the look-elsewhere count, on average 5.5 thresholds per +-150 MeV window; isospin and G parity are not imposed.
Threshold proximity is the standard signature of hadronic molecules and of threshold cusps in QCD; it supports the molecular branch of H8 only in the sense that H8 includes that branch.
Lattice QCD results for T_bb scatter from 83 to 189 MeV binding; the comparison is not a measurement.
